tasks.short: Write and check specifications for HR reports so developers build the right measures, access controls and checks.

today.trigger: A manager requests a new report, or an AFAS field, HR policy or dashboard definition changes.
steps: Clarify the business question, audience and decision the report should support.
Trace fields through AFAS extracts and relevant Recruitee or Studytube records.
Specify joins, calculations, refresh timing, access permissions and acceptance checks.
Review the specification with the requester and report developer.
Record the approved version and resolve questions during development.
systems: Power BI and its semantic model
drudgery: Rewriting standard sections on refreshes and permissions.
Checking that specifications match current measures.
today.time_sinks: Finding authoritative definitions and resolving inconsistent treatment of transfers, rehires, flex workers and day-90 outcomes. Actual task duration needs measurement.

lenses.faster: Manual transcription and first-draft formatting disappear; the analyst checks lineage, definitions and acceptance examples. As a planning estimate, each 100 minutes today becomes 55 minutes: 15 preparing inputs, 25 reviewing and correcting, and 15 agreeing the specification.
lenses.autonomous: An approved report request starts document assembly from versioned definitions and schemas. The assistant drafts the specification and flags gaps; the analyst approves it before development starts.
lenses.ambitious: New service: give the Controller a shared specification connecting payroll cost with hiring cohorts and day-90 retention. Demand would grow as specifications become cheaper, particularly when Finance and HR currently reconcile different totals.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying schema details and chasing document versions. The analyst gets more time to settle what productive after 90 days actually means with site managers.
lenses.options: Compare definitions that handle site transfers, rehires and missing productivity assessments differently, with worked examples. Those alternatives can change which hiring cohorts appear successful and what managers decide to improve.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward metric design sessions and acceptance reviews; with delegated authority, the analyst can reject inconsistent definitions and unsuitable access requests. The job becomes more expert because it combines data modelling, employment context and privacy judgment.
reach: Absorb the FP&A Analyst's drafting of workforce-cost reporting requirements after learning AFAS ledger mappings, accruals and reconciliation; Finance retains approval of accounting treatment.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst must resolve competing meanings of success, spot misleading measures and negotiate definitions with managers who understand warehouse work, CAO arrangements and seasonal staffing.
tasks.pattern_why: Document drafting is predictable, but defining the report requires business judgment and discussion. A person-led workflow with a fixed drafting step is sufficient.

in_practice.trigger: An approved reporting request or a reviewed change to a source schema or metric definition.
steps: Load the request, approved template, schema metadata and existing metric definitions.
Draft the specification, marking missing information and linking each definition to its source.
Generate worked calculation examples and proposed acceptance checks.
Have the analyst verify joins, populations, CAO implications and access controls.
Agree unresolved choices with the requester and publish the approved version.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every specification; the business owner accepts the metric meaning, and Finance approves accounting definitions. Seek OR consent before implementing changes that require it.
data_needed: Versioned source schemas and field descriptions.
Existing DAX measures and approved metric definitions.
Synthetic calculation examples covering transfers, rehires and flex workers.
Relevant CAO provisions and recorded privacy or OR decisions.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history with source versions, unresolved questions, reviewer decisions and final approval.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot can write DAX and summarise reports, but requires a prepared semantic model to reduce misinterpretation.
Drafting specifications from approved templates and schema metadata is feasible; the proposed end-to-end saving is an estimate without a Noordhaven case.
WOR Article 27 covers arrangements for employee personal data and facilities capable of observing attendance, behaviour or performance.

risks: Plausible but incorrect joins or cohort definitions could distort 90-day retention and payroll cost.
Outdated schema metadata could produce a specification that developers cannot implement.
A report could enable employee monitoring beyond its stated purpose; assess access, purpose and OR consent requirements before implementation.
Absence specifications must exclude medical causes and restrict access to permitted absence information.
research_questions: How much specification time goes into transcription versus resolving business definitions, and does a pilot achieve the estimated saving after review?
Can Noordhaven export current schema and semantic-model metadata with dependable version identifiers?
Do worked examples reveal every material difference in treatment of rehires, transfers, flex workers and incomplete day-90 assessments?
Which proposed reports require OR consent, and who can formally approve metric definitions and access?

tasks.short: Track HR technology changes and recommend practical improvements to hiring, onboarding and reporting.

today.trigger: A periodic technology review, vendor announcement or recurring HR problem prompts a search for better tools.
steps: Identify a hiring, onboarding or reporting problem worth investigating.
Read vendor announcements, product documentation and customer evidence.
Check compatibility with AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and Microsoft 365.
Assess cost, privacy, OR requirements and likely operational benefit.
Write a recommendation and discuss whether to run a pilot.
drudgery: Reading repeated announcements about the same feature.
Separating product availability from promised outcomes.
Reformatting links and claims into briefing notes.
today.time_sinks: Finding credible evidence and testing whether a feature works with Noordhaven's stack and shift workforce. Actual review duration needs measurement.

lenses.faster: First-pass reading, deduplication and briefing drafts disappear; source verification and local feasibility assessment stay. As a planning estimate, each 100 minutes today becomes 45 minutes: 15 checking sources, 20 assessing fit and 10 discussing the recommendation.
lenses.autonomous: A weekly scan of approved sources starts the workflow, which groups announcements and drafts evidence-backed recommendations. The analyst checks consequential claims and approves the briefing before anyone acts on it.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: choose weekly whether a specific hiring or onboarding bottleneck merits a small technology experiment, rather than waiting for a periodic review. Demand would grow as screening gets cheaper, but site managers' capacity to run useful pilots remains limited.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rereading vendor claims and assembling link lists. The analyst gets more time with recruiters and shift managers to test whether a proposed change solves their problem.
lenses.options: Compare improving the existing stack, adding a product and changing the process without buying software. This can change the investment decision when an integration or simpler workflow offers more value than a new tool.
lenses.altitude: The week includes a short evidence review and pilot discussions tied to time to hire, week-one onboarding and retention. With delegated authority, the analyst can reject unsupported proposals and select candidates within an agreed pilot budget; the role becomes more expert in evaluation and implementation.
reach: Absorb the Recruiter's first-pass assessment of recruitment software after learning the hiring workflow, candidate experience and fair-selection requirements; the Recruiter retains hiring and candidate decisions.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst must judge whether evidence transfers to Dutch logistics, understand night-shift and flex-worker constraints, and challenge vendors through direct conversations and practical pilots.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed workflow can collect approved sources and use one model call to produce a structured, checkable briefing. Open-ended agent activity is unnecessary.

in_practice.trigger: A weekly schedule or an analyst-selected operational problem.
steps: Collect recent material from an approved source list and remove duplicates.
Generate a briefing with source links, exact claims, evidence strength and unanswered questions.
Compare each relevant change against Noordhaven's stack, workforce access and North Star inputs.
Have the analyst verify claims and assess licensing, privacy, OR and applicable AI Act requirements.
Approve a recommendation with a pilot measure, owner and stop condition.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every briefing and pilot recommendation. HR leadership approves spend and operational changes; relevant privacy and OR processes precede deployment.
data_needed: Current product versions, licences and integration capabilities.
Approved source list and dated source material.
Prioritised HR bottlenecks and baseline input metrics.
Privacy requirements, workforce access needs and relevant OR decisions.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint evidence register with retrieved sources, claim checks, analyst edits, recommendations and subsequent pilot results.

evidence.claim: Microsoft describes an HR insights agent and explicitly cautions that faster access to information does not itself improve decisions.
Power BI Copilot provides relevant capabilities in Noordhaven's stack, subject to capacity and semantic-model requirements; non-English chat is not officially supported.

Uber reports QueryGPT reducing query preparation from about ten to three minutes, while describing unresolved hallucinated tables and columns; this is evidence for query assistance, not Noordhaven's trend-review saving.
A model can draft sourced technology summaries inside a fixed review workflow; the estimated saving requires a local pilot.

risks: Vendor claims could be presented as proven customer outcomes or transferred to Noordhaven without supporting evidence.
A summary could omit licensing, integration or Dutch-language limitations that make a proposal impractical.
Low-cost screening could create more pilot work than recruiters and site managers can absorb.
Employee scoring or monitoring proposals may trigger GDPR, OR and AI Act requirements; checking the applicable scope and timetable is part of feasibility assessment.
research_questions: Does the weekly briefing find useful changes beyond those already noticed by system owners, after source-checking time is counted?
Which shortlisted features are available under Noordhaven's actual licences and supported integrations?
Can a pilot measure improvement in a named North Star input without relying on vendor claims or self-reported AI use?
Can warehouse staff, night shifts and agency flex workers access the proposed service, and what legal or OR conditions apply?

role.altitude: The role becomes the authority for consistent HR measures and credible technology evaluation. Its week centres on metric decisions, report acceptance and measured pilots, with delegated rights to approve reporting definitions, reject misleading outputs and prioritise pilot candidates.
reach: Draft workforce-cost reporting requirements for the FP&A Analyst after learning ledger mappings and reconciliation.
Screen recruitment technology for the Recruiter after learning candidate workflows and fair-selection requirements.
Design onboarding and certificate reporting requirements for the Learning and Development Specialist after learning Studytube records and site-specific certification rules.
role.ceiling_note: These two tasks account for 96.2 hours annually; the estimates release about 47.8 hours, including review. Wider role savings cannot be inferred from them, and expansion is limited by integration access, stakeholder decisions and capacity to run pilots.
skills_to_grow: Power BI semantic modelling, DAX and SQL validation.
Cohort definitions linking recruitment, onboarding and day-90 outcomes.
AFAS finance mappings and workforce-cost reconciliation.
Source verification, pilot design and evaluation of operational results.
Dutch CAO interpretation, GDPR, OR consent processes and applicable EU AI Act requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Provide HR leadership and site managers with trusted hiring-to-day-90 measures and a small portfolio of tested improvements, extending visibility to flex workers and night shifts where access and lawful data sharing permit. Use verified results to decide which changes deserve wider rollout.
